Bank of America Corporation BAC is strengthening its international banking franchise through significant expansion in Switzerland, where it recently marked 75 years of operations. The bank's Swiss corporate banking client base has tripled since January 2024, with client numbers increasing nearly 30% year to date. Further, since the launch of its Swiss growth initiative in 2021, the local workforce has doubled, reflecting continued investments in its international business.

Bank of America is expanding its Swiss operations by strengthening Financial Institutions Group (FIG) coverage, broadening corporate banking capabilities and growing its middle-market offering. The bank's local business spans mergers and acquisitions (M&A) advisory, equity and debt capital markets, corporate banking and Global Markets.

BAC has advised on several significant transactions involving Swiss companies over the past 18 months, including deals involving Lonza, ABB, Nestlé, Galderma, DocMorris and Swisscom. The bank has also strengthened its capital markets presence by underwriting equity and debt offerings, including Galderma's secondary accelerated bookbuild and bond offerings for Swisscom, Nestlé and Novartis.

The expansion aligns with Bank of America's broader international middle-market strategy, which initially gained traction in Switzerland and has since expanded into the United Kingdom, Ireland, Italy and Germany. The initiative provides companies with access to financing, treasury, payments and foreign exchange solutions, strengthening the bank's ability to serve businesses across multiple markets. Continued investments in local teams and broader client coverage should help deepen corporate relationships, generate cross-border business opportunities and diversify revenue streams.

BAC's investment banking fees increased 14.6% year over year in the first nine months of 2026, reflecting a recovery in capital markets activity. Although third-quarter investment banking fees, excluding self-led deals, declined 11% year over year, the bank remains focused on strengthening its advisory and capital markets capabilities. Continued international expansion and a growing corporate client base could support future advisory mandates, financing transactions and fee income generation.

Over the past three months, shares of BAC have declined 20.6%, underperforming the industry's 15.4% decline.

title: GS vs. C: Which Bank Stock Deserves a Spot in Your Portfolio?

GS vs. C: Which Bank Stock Deserves a Spot in Your Portfolio?
Riya Anand

GS
C
Explore stocks on Coinbase
Trading disclosure

The U.S. banking industry is benefiting from resilient dealmaking activity, robust trading revenues and growing demand for wealth and asset management services, despite lingering macroeconomic and interest rate uncertainties. Against this backdrop, The Goldman Sachs Group, Inc. GS and Citigroup, Inc. C stand out as two prominent banking giants well-positioned to capitalize on these favorable industry trends.

While Goldman is leveraging its investment banking dominance, strong trading franchise and expanding asset and wealth management business to drive earnings growth, Citigroup is focused on business simplification, operational efficiency and strengthening its core banking, services and wealth franchises to improve profitability.

With both banking behemoths pursuing distinct growth strategies and enhancing shareholder value, which stock offers a more compelling investment opportunity at present?

The Case for GS

Goldman has long maintained a leading position in mergers and acquisitions (M&A), trading and capital markets. Under CEO David Solomon, the company has strategically shifted away from non-core consumer banking operations to focus on its core strengths in investment banking (IB), trading, and asset and wealth management (AWM). These efforts continue to yield favorable results, with Global Banking & Markets revenues rising 34% year over year to $41.72 billion in the first nine months of 2026, supported by a 40% increase in IB fees, a 57% surge in equities revenues and a 6% rise in fixed income, currency and commodities (FICC) revenues. A rebound in M&A activity, robust underwriting volumes and sustained client engagement are expected to support the segment's growth, though a modest decline in the IB fee backlog as of September 2026 compared with December 2025 warrants monitoring.

Goldman has been actively reshaping its portfolio through strategic acquisitions and divestitures. In August 2026, GS agreed to acquire LCN Capital Partners and NEOS Investments, strengthening its alternative real estate investment capabilities and expanding its presence in options-based exchange-traded funds (ETFs), respectively. These followed the acquisitions of Innovator Capital Management in April and Industry Ventures in January. Further, the divestiture of its Polish asset management business and the planned transition of its Apple Card program to JPMorgan Chase underscore Goldman's commitment to streamlining operations and directing resources toward higher-return businesses.

title: Citigroup considers return to Venezuela after five-year exit – report
detail:
Citigroup considers return to Venezuela after five-year exit – report
Citi withdrew from Venezuela in 2021.Credit: Samuel Boivin/ Shutterstock.com. · Retail Banker International · Samuel Boivin/ Shutterstock.com.
Vidhya Edwards Munnangi
Thu, November 26, 2026 at 6:40 AM EST 2 min read
C
Trade C on Coinbase
Trading disclosure

Citigroup is considering re-entering Venezuela's banking market, five years after ending its operations in the country, reported Bloomberg citing sources.

Citi executives are discussing a potential return with Trump administration officials at the US State Department and Treasury, sources told the publication.

The discussions include the structure of any re-entry and the sanctions waivers that may be required. Other banks have also approached US officials about returning to Venezuela, one person said.

Citi is expected to begin with correspondent banking relationships involving financial institutions already operating in Venezuela, rather than reopening local operations immediately.

Two people said the bank is not currently planning an on-the-ground presence.

The issue has relevance for Citi chief executive Jane Fraser, who led the bank's Latin America business from Miami between 2015 and 2019.

In her first year leading the Latin America business, Citi entered a four-year swaps contract with Venezuela. The bank provided the country with a $1.1bn loan secured against gold collateral.

Venezuela's central bank later missed a deadline to repurchase the gold. Citigroup sold the metal and transferred about $260m to a US account formerly controlled by Venezuela's central bank.

Fraser addressed Venezuela at a Bloomberg conference in New York in September.

She said a lasting change in the country would likely require changes in both leadership and policy. Delcy Rodriguez has led Venezuela since Maduro's capture by the US.

"The government is the same government who has been there for a while, and in my experience, you often need to have a personnel change and a change in agenda if you're really going to make it enduring," Fraser said.

In 2021, Citigroup sold its Venezuela operations to Banco Nacional de Crédito and took steps to protect local executives during the exit. Citi opened branches in Venezuela in 1917 and previously employed hundreds of people in the country.

"Citigroup considers return to Venezuela after five-year exit – report" was originally created and published by Retail Banker International, a GlobalData owned brand.

Key Takeaways

Citi reiterated its Buy rating and $1,050 target on Seagate after the latest drop, 122% above a Nov. 25 close that sits 57% below the June closing high.

Storage stocks sold off on AI-spending and flash-price worries, while Seagate and Western Digital both guided to more growth.

Analysts raised Seagate's fiscal 2028 earnings estimates through the selloff, and $1,050 is 16x those earnings.

The call looks right, but fiscal 2028 depends on drive prices Seagate hasn't agreed with customers yet.

Seagate Technology (STX:NASDAQ) is down 57% from its June closing high, and Citi thinks it can more than double from here. Citi's Asiya Merchant has reiterated her Buy rating and $1,050 target since the selloff deepened, 122% above the Nov. 25 close of $472.33.

Sandisk (SNDK:NASDAQ) fell 16% on Nov. 20, a day after TrendForce said it expects NAND flash contract prices to start falling in early 2027. Meanwhile, Western Digital (WDC:NASDAQ), Seagate's main hard-drive rival, guided its non-GAAP gross margin to 60%-61% for the December quarter, up from 58.1%.

Three Reasons Investors Sold Seagate

On Oct. 2, Nikkei reported that Toshiba plans to double its hard-drive capacity. Seagate's record September quarter then showed 198 exabytes of nearline shipments, barely above June's 195. On Nov. 5, the stock sank 16% in a post-midterm AI selloff after a lawmaker called for a pause on advanced AI development. And while TrendForce's forecast covered flash, Seagate tied part of its June-quarter Edge IoT growth to rising flash prices.

Citi Is Betting on the Contracts

Merchant cut her target to $1,050 from $1,300 on Oct. 28 and has reiterated it since, with the stock far lower. When she raised it in late July, she wrote that "demand remains exceptionally strong on hyperscalers, AI workloads, and growing data retention," according to GuruFocus.

Most of Seagate's nearline supply is allocated through calendar 2028, with prices set through 2027, and it guides December-quarter revenue to $4.8 billion, up 70% at the midpoint.

Evercore ISI cut its target to $700 from $1,000 on Nov. 24, though it kept its Outperform rating and said the selloff "might have overextended."

Does $1,050 Add Up for Seagate Stock?

The average target is $1,023, up from $293 a year ago, and the stock trades below even the lowest, $520.

Estimates kept rising through the selloff. Fiscal 2028 EPS, for the year to June 2028, rose to $64.44 from $55.37 over 90 days.

Key Takeaways

Citi reiterated its Buy rating and $1,300 target on Micron on Nov. 23, 106% above the stock's latest close, after a 48% drop from its June high.

Citi argues the memory selloff has gone too far, estimating that even a full stop to Nvidia-linked financing would cut DRAM demand only about 12%.

On fiscal 2028 consensus earnings, $1,300 is 6.3x, well under the roughly 10x Micron has usually traded at, and SK hynix is priced even lower than Micron.

The call holds up because it needs only fiscal 2028 earnings near consensus and a below-average multiple, and Micron's mid-December report is the next test.

Micron Technology (MU:NASDAQ) has lost 48% from its June high, and Citi thinks the market has overshot. On Nov. 23, analyst Atif Malik reiterated his Buy rating and $1,300 target, 106% above the stock's Nov. 24 close of $629.79.

SK hynix (SKHY:NASDAQ) and Sandisk (SNDK:NASDAQ) sold off on the same worries, and the market prices all three as if their profits have peaked.

Shortage doubts sank it

Investors doubt the memory shortage will last, and November gave them three reasons. In mid-November, the Wall Street Journal reported that Nvidia's new leadership planned to scale back the financing it gives AI customers. On Nov. 22, Goldman Sachs said it now expects DRAM prices to fall 19% in 2028, up from 5%, and cut its 2028 earnings estimate for SK hynix by 23%. And on Nov. 24, BNP Paribas Exane's Karl Ackerman downgraded Micron to Neutral and cut his target to $775 from $1,700, seeing supply and demand reach parity from mid-2027.

TIKR tracks 49 analysts on Micron. How many say "Buy"?

See the full breakdown of Buy, Hold, and Sell ratings on Micron, along with Wall Street's revenue and earnings estimates, all in one place. More than 500,000 investors use TIKR to research stocks like this one. See Micron's Analyst Ratings

Citi says the shortage outlasts the fear

Malik set his $1,300 target in September and has held it through the selloff. His latest note put a number on the Nvidia worry: "We estimate only ~12%/7% impact on total DRAM/NAND demand, even if we assume Nvidia-related financing initiatives were to cease completely."

He also argues that new fabs take years to build, so DRAM stays tight through 2028. Micron's numbers back the near end: over 75% of its 2027 output is committed, and it guided first-quarter revenue to $61.5 billion, up from $54.2 billion last quarter. Malik made the same case for Sandisk, with a $262.50 target.

Does $1,300 add up?

The consensus target among the 49 analysts who rate Micron on TIKR has gone from $220 a year ago to $1,530, 143% above the price. Citi sits about 15% below that.

title: Citigroup Eyes Venezuela Re-Entry: Can It Grow Cross-Border Payments?
detail:
Citigroup Eyes Venezuela Re-Entry: Can It Grow Cross-Border Payments?
Riya Anand
Wed, November 25, 2026 at 9:20 AM EST 3 min read
C
JPM
HSBC
Explore stocks on Coinbase
Trading disclosure

Citigroup, Inc. C is weighing a return to Venezuela that could extend the reach of its cross-border payments business, according to Reuters, which was published on Yahoo Finance.

Citigroup, which sold its remaining Venezuelan operations in 2021, would likely start by establishing correspondent banking relationships with local lenders. Initially, the bank would likely focus on correspondent banking ties with local financial companies rather than immediately establishing a physical presence.

For C's Treasury and Trade Solutions (TTS) business, the immediate opportunity would be to earn fees on payment processing and dollar clearing. Local bank relationships could help Citigroup serve existing multinational clients that need to pay suppliers or collect payments tied to Venezuela. Over time, those relationships could also create opportunities to sell cash management services.

The potential return comes as Citigroup's payments business is already growing. In the first nine months of 2026, the bank's cross-border transaction value rose 12% year over year to $336.4 billion, while U.S. dollar clearing volume increased 4% to 137.3 million payment instructions. These figures illustrate the scale of C's existing payments network.

In the first nine months of 2026, C's TTS revenues rose 17% year over year to $14.26 billion. Noninterest revenues increased 12% to $3.62 billion, driven in part by higher fees and increased transaction activity. Across Citigroup's broader Services segment, Latin America generated $2.26 billion in revenues, up 15% year over year. A return to Venezuela could give C another opportunity to build on its existing regional business.

What Would Make Venezuela Re-Entry Pay Off for Citigroup?

The financial upside hinges on which transactions Citigroup can process and how much recurring volume it can attract. A narrow set of permitted activities could limit fee income, while screening counterparties and monitoring payments would add costs.

Citigroup's return to Venezuela could grow its cross-border payments business if it can sign local banking partners and attract recurring dollar-clearing and payment flows from existing multinational clients. The scope of permitted transactions will determine how much volume C can capture. If the resulting fees cover compliance and operating costs, Venezuela could make a modest contribution to Services earnings.

Other Banks Expanding Cross-Border Payments

HSBC Holdings HSBC and JPMorgan Chase JPM are also expanding payment capabilities to strengthen cross-border transactions, liquidity management and corporate client relationships.
